questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them.
Encourage them to take less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Encourage friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.
Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when you use them together.

questions.question: If you are drinking alcohol and plan to ride later, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than usual.
Allow at least an hour for each drink to leave your system before riding.
Exercise or dance to wear the drinks off.
Drink hot coffee to become more alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow at least an hour for each drink to leave your system before riding.
questions.explanation: The only way to remove alcohol from your system is to wait. Your body processes about one drink per hour. Riding after drinking is dangerous, even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding where sand and gravel have collected on a paved road, you should:

options.text: Downshift and use more throttle.
Pull in the clutch.
Use only the rear brake to slow down.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces with sand and gravel, do not make sudden changes in speed or direction. Be extra careful on surfaces that do not grip well.

questions.question: When riding with passengers, you should:

options.text: Start slowing sooner than you would if riding alone.
Use only your front brake to slow.
Never talk to them.
Start in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing sooner than you would if riding alone.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This means it takes longer to slow down with a passenger than without one. Start braking earlier when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: When consumed together, the effects of alcohol and drugs:

options.text: Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is consumed alone.
Are usually minimal.
Often balance out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be more pronounced than when either is consumed alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes the effects even more dangerous.

questions.question: When checking your motorcycle before riding, make sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause some friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: To be seen at night, it is best to wear:

options.text: Light clothing.
A white helmet.
Reflective clothing.
A red jacket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing with reflective materials to be more visible at night.

questions.question: When preparing to pass on the left, it is best to:

options.text: Signal, check your left mirror, look left, and move into the passing lane.
Signal, immediately move into the passing lane, and accelerate.
Signal, check your left mirror, and move into the passing lane.
Signal, accelerate, and move into the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your left mirror, look left, and move into the passing lane.
questions.explanation: To pass a vehicle on the left, signal first. Check your left mirror and look over your shoulder. When it is safe, move into the passing lane and accelerate past the other vehicle quickly. Signal again and check before moving back to your original lane.

questions.question: For greatest safety, your helmet should:

options.text: Fit tightly at the base and loosely at the top.
Fit loosely all the way around.
Fit snugly all the way around.
Be worn only on long rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly all the way around.
questions.explanation: Helmets should fit snugly all the way around. Wear a helmet every time you ride. Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Makes a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear while riding.
Protects you in a crash.
Should not be worn while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: You should wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally made of leather, when riding. Leather jackets help protect you in a crash. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: The proper body position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Lets you sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Makes you lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keeps your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This lets you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can:

options.text: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
See only the lane behind you.
See only the lane next to you.
See most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A properly adjusted mirror may show a little of your arm or shoulder, but seeing the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce injuries in a crash?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride it like your bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different, so check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding an unfamiliar bike. Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before you ride.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Polyester
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the most protection when riding.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while turning or riding a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten the motorcycle first, then brake.
Brake first, then try to straighten the motorcycle.
Only brake and not worry about straightening.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the motorcycle first, then brake.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly while turning or in a curve, straighten the motorcycle first, then brake. Motorcycles have less traction when leaning in a turn or curve.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for proper protection while riding.

questions.question: For the most protection, choose a helmet that:

options.text: Fits loosely.
Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Has survived a previous crash.
Provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the most protection. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: Which of the following should you check before each ride?

options.text: The wear and tread on your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has
The shine of your paint
The wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread on your tires
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your motorcycle thoroughly. Inspect the tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.
